title: Uses of Earth Materials by People

competencies.text: Describe properties and local availability of rocks, minerals, and soils. Explain how they are harnessed for industries.

days.title: Rocks, Minerals & Soils
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to distinguish rocks, minerals, and soils; describe the three rock types; identify common Philippine minerals and their uses; and explain how earth materials are harnessed for industry.

🪨 Rocks vs. Minerals vs. Soils

TermDefinitionExample
MineralA naturally occurring, inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and crystal structureQuartz, gold, calcite, feldspar
RockA naturally occurring solid made of one or more mineralsGranite (quartz + feldspar + mica), limestone (calcite)
SoilLoose mixture of weathered rock, minerals, organic matter, water, and airLoam, clay, sand

🔬 Properties Used to Identify Minerals

PropertyWhat It Tests
HardnessResistance to scratching (Mohs scale 1–10)
Color & streakColor of mineral in solid form vs. when rubbed on a plate
LusterHow it reflects light — metallic, glassy, dull, pearly
Cleavage & fractureHow it breaks along flat planes or irregularly
Specific gravityDensity compared to water
Reaction to acidEffervescence (fizzing) in acid — identifies carbonates like calcite

🪨 The Three Rock Types

Rock TypeHow It FormsExampleUses
IgneousCooling and solidifying of magma or lavaGranite, basalt, obsidianBuilding stone, countertops, gravel
SedimentaryCompaction and cementation of sediments (or chemical precipitation)Limestone, sandstone, shaleCement, building stone, chalk
MetamorphicExisting rock changed by heat and pressureMarble (from limestone), slate (from shale)Marble for flooring & sculpture; slate for roofing

💎 Common Philippine Minerals & Their Uses

MineralLocation in PHUses
GoldBaguio, Benguet, Surigao, MasbateJewelry, electronics, coins, dentistry
CopperToledo (Cebu), Mankayan, SurigaoElectrical wiring, plumbing, electronics
NickelSurigao, Palawan, ZambalesStainless steel, batteries, coins
ChromiteZambales, SurigaoStainless steel, refractory bricks
IronBulacan, Camarines Norte, SurigaoSteel, construction, machinery
LimestoneRizal, Cebu, Palawan, BulacanCement, chalk, building stone, glass
MarbleRomblonSculpture, flooring, tiles
Silica / QuartzVariousGlass, electronics, sandpaper
CoalSemirara (Antique), Cebu, SurigaoElectricity generation, fuel
Salt (halite)Pangasinan (asinan), MindoroFood, water softeners, chemistry

🌾 Soil — The Foundation of Agriculture

Soil TypePropertiesBest For
SandyLarge particles, drains fast, low nutrientsRoot crops (carrots, cassava)
ClaySmall particles, holds water, compactPottery, rice paddies (with irrigation)
LoamBalanced mix — best for most cropsRice, corn, vegetables, fruit trees

🏭 How Earth Materials Are Harnessed for Industry

IndustryEarth Materials Used
ConstructionLimestone (cement), marble, granite, sand, gravel
ElectronicsCopper, gold, silicon (quartz), rare earth metals
EnergyCoal, geothermal (heat from Earth's interior), natural gas
AgricultureSoil, limestone (for neutralizing acid), phosphate rock (fertilizer)
JewelryGold, silver, pearls, diamonds
CeramicsClay, kaolin, feldspar
GlassSilica sand, limestone, soda ash

⚠️ Environmental Impact of Mining

  • Deforestation: Clearing land for mining operations
  • Water pollution: Acid mine drainage into rivers
  • Soil erosion: Exposed land loses topsoil
  • Habitat destruction: Ecosystems disrupted
  • Social impact: Displacement of Indigenous communities

Solutions: Sustainable mining practices, rehabilitation of mined areas, strict regulation (DENR-MGB), and support for renewable alternatives.

📌 Quick Check

  • What is the difference between a rock and a mineral? (Answer: rocks are made of one or more minerals)
  • How are igneous rocks formed? (Answer: cooling and solidifying of magma or lava)
  • What mineral is used in cement? (Answer: limestone)

days.title: Match Game — Earth Materials
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each earth material, rock type, or concept to its correct description or use. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Naturally occurring inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition
Forms from cooling and solidifying of magma or lava
Forms from compaction and cementation of sediments — like limestone
Forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure — like marble
Used to make cement, chalk, and building stone
Used in electrical wiring, plumbing, and electronics
Balanced mix of sand, silt, and clay — best for most crops
Used for sculpture, flooring, and tiles

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Industry Uses
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🏗️ A construction company needs cement for a new bridge. Which earth material is the MAIN ingredient?

choices.label: A) Limestone — heated to produce lime, the key ingredient in cement

scenario.text: 💻 A tech company builds a new factory for electronics. Which minerals from the Philippines would they most likely need?

choices.label: A) Copper, gold, and silica (for wiring, contacts, and semiconductors)

scenario.text: 🌾 A farmer complains that their soil drains too quickly and doesn't hold nutrients. What type of soil are they likely using?

choices.label: A) Sandy soil — large particles drain fast and hold few nutrients

scenario.text: ⛏️ A mining company opens a copper mine in Surigao. What environmental impact should be carefully managed?

choices.label: A) Acid mine drainage, deforestation, and habitat destruction
C) Cooling of the local climate

scenario.text: 🏺 A potter in Vigan wants to make traditional clay pots. Which soil type is BEST?

choices.label: A) Clay — small particles that hold shape and harden when fired

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Geology Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Geology Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?

choices.label: A) Rocks are made of one or more minerals; minerals have a definite chemical composition
B) Rocks are harder than minerals
C) Minerals are bigger than rocks
A) Cooling and solidifying of magma or lava
C) Heat and pressure on existing rocks

escape.text: Which rock type is formed from heat and pressure on existing rocks?
Which mineral is used to make cement?
Which soil type is BEST for most crops?

choices.label: A) Loam — balanced mix of sand, silt, and clay
